Series::clear_sensitivity¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::clear_sensitivity() const -> void

What It Does¶

clear_sensitivity() removes the currently stored reverse-mode sensitivity from this Series.

That is a narrower operation than many readers first assume.

It does:

  • forget the stored sensitivity value, if one exists

It does not:

  • disable tracks_slope()

  • alter the actual numeric data in the Series

  • rewrite the graph that future operations build from this value

So the right mental model is “clear the stored sensitivity state,” not “detach this series from reverse-mode entirely.”

Parameters¶

None.

This is a state-reset operation on self.

Returns¶

void The method mutates the stored autograd state and does not return a value.

When To Use It¶

clear_sensitivity() is most useful in three situations:

  • you want to inspect one reverse pass, then discard it before the next one

  • you are reusing a tracked leaf across separate computations and want a clean sensitivity buffer

  • you want has_sensitivity() to become false again without disabling tracking

That last point is important. Clearing stored sensitivity and turning tracking off are separate controls.

Examples¶

Example 1. After a reverse pass, clear_sensitivity() removes the stored sensitivity and has_sensitivity() becomes false again.

auto life = pluss::make_series({2.0, 4.0, 8.0});
life.tracks_slope_(true);

std::cout << "before=" << (life.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
life.log().sum().reverse();
std::cout << "after_reverse=" << (life.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
life.clear_sensitivity();
std::cout << "after_clear=" << (life.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

before=false
after_reverse=true
after_clear=false

Example 2. Clearing between passes lets the next reverse pass start from an empty stored sensitivity buffer.

auto reuse = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
reuse.tracks_slope_(true);

reuse.mul(2.0).sum().reverse();
std::cout << "first=" << reuse.sensitivity() << "\n";

reuse.clear_sensitivity();
reuse.mul(5.0).sum().reverse();
std::cout << "second=" << reuse.sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

first=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[2, 2, 2]
second=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[5, 5, 5]

The second pass is not added on top of the first one because the stored sensitivity was cleared before it ran.

Example 3. Clearing stored sensitivity does not disable tracking.

auto keep_track = pluss::make_series({9.0, 10.0});
keep_track.tracks_slope_(true);
keep_track.mul(4.0).sum().reverse();
keep_track.clear_sensitivity();

std::cout << "tracks=" << (keep_track.tracks_slope() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";
std::cout << "has_dx=" << (keep_track.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

tracks=true
has_dx=false

That distinction matters in long-lived code. The leaf is still configured to participate in future reverse passes even though its current stored sensitivity was discarded.

Example 4. Calling clear_sensitivity() on a series that does not currently store sensitivity is a harmless no-op.

auto noop = pluss::make_series({7.0, 8.0});
noop.clear_sensitivity();
std::cout << "has_dx=" << (noop.has_sensitivity() ? "true" : "false") << "\n";

Output¶

has_dx=false

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • clear_sensitivity() does not turn tracking off. Use tracks_slope_ for that.

  • Clearing stored sensitivity does not change the forward values.

  • This method is about the current stored result of reverse-mode, not about future graph construction.

Summary¶

Use clear_sensitivity() when you want to forget the current stored sensitivity while keeping the Series itself and its tracking configuration intact.

See Also¶

  • Series::has_sensitivity: test whether a stored sensitivity currently exists.

  • Series::sensitivity: read the stored value itself.

  • Series::tracks_slope_: enable or disable tracking.
